content.user_title: Configure Repositories for Matt Pocock Skills
content.value_statement: Engineering skills need consistent repository conventions before they can manage work reliably. This skill gathers user choices and creates the required agent guidance files.
actual_capabilities: Inspects repository guidance, remotes, context files, ADR folders, and previous setup output.
Guides users through issue tracker, pull request triage, label vocabulary, and domain layout decisions one section at a time.
Supports GitHub, GitLab, local Markdown, and user-defined issue tracking workflows.
Drafts an Agent skills section and three repository guidance documents before writing.
Updates existing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md guidance without duplicating its managed section.
Uses provided tracker, triage label, and domain templates to create repository-specific documentation.
limitations: Requires interactive decisions and explicit confirmation before writing files.
Does not create or migrate issues, labels, domain models, or ADRs.
Remote tracker commands require separately installed and authenticated GitHub or GitLab CLI tools.
Custom trackers are recorded as freeform instructions without validating an integration.

use_cases.title: Set Up a Solo Repository
use_cases.description: Configure local Markdown issues, default triage states, and one domain context without requiring a hosted tracker.

use_cases.title: Standardize Maintainer Workflows
use_cases.description: Document GitHub or GitLab issue handling, external contribution triage, and the repository's established label names.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Monorepo
use_cases.description: Record multiple domain contexts, shared ADR locations, and tracker conventions for engineering agents working across packages.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Repository Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up this repository for Matt Pocock's engineering skills. Explain each decision simply and ask one question at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the repository has not been configured for these skills.

prompt_templates.title: GitHub Workflow Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this GitHub repository and prepare its issue tracker, triage labels, and single-context documentation. Show every draft before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a standard GitHub repository with one domain context.

prompt_templates.title: GitLab Workflow Reconciliation
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure this GitLab project with our existing labels and external merge request triage disabled. Preserve current agent guidance outside the managed section.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when setup must respect existing GitLab and guidance conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Monorepo Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure this monorepo for [tracker] using multiple domain contexts and our custom label mapping. Reconcile existing setup files and propose only necessary changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an established monorepo with custom tracker and domain conventions.

output_examples.input: Set up this GitHub repository with default labels and one domain context.
output_examples.output: Prepared drafts for the existing agent guidance file and three repository setup documents. Awaiting confirmation before writing.

output_examples.input: Use local Markdown issues and preserve our custom triage labels.
output_examples.output: Configured local issue storage, recorded the five label mappings, and documented the single-context domain layout.

output_examples.input: Configure a GitLab monorepo without merge request triage.
output_examples.output: Documented GitLab issue handling, disabled merge request triage, and mapped multiple domain contexts through the repository context map.

best_practices: Review each proposed decision and draft before allowing file changes.
Match label mappings to labels that already exist in the selected tracker.
Re-run the skill only when tracker or repository structure conventions change.
anti_patterns: Do not skip inspection of existing guidance and setup documents.
Do not enable external contribution triage unless maintainers use pull requests as a request surface.
Do not overwrite surrounding user guidance or create both supported agent guidance files.

faq.question: Is this skill a script?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-driven workflow that inspects the repository, asks for decisions, presents drafts, and then writes approved files.

faq.question: Which issue trackers are supported?
faq.answer: It provides templates for GitHub, GitLab, and local Markdown. Other trackers can be documented through user-supplied workflow instructions.

faq.question: Which agent guidance file does it edit?
faq.answer: If CLAUDE.md exists, the skill edits it. Otherwise, it edits AGENTS.md or asks which file to create.

faq.question: Does it create tracker labels?
faq.answer: No. It records mappings for existing label names so later skills can use the correct vocabulary.

faq.question: Can I run the setup again?
faq.answer: Yes. Re-run it when changing trackers or rebuilding the setup, then review every proposed update.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose the multi-context layout, which records a root context map and per-context domain files.
